title: ChatGPT sign-in: what changes on the day we switch to OpenAI's official version

steps.path: Settings → Assistant settings → Cloud providers → ChatGPT, while signed in
steps.headline: Signed in on the official version, the card loses its usage bars and plan name and gains a Manage usage button.
steps.changed: The 5-hour and weekly bars and the plan name ("ChatGPT Plus") are gone: OpenAI won't give them to apps on this version. My Account becomes Manage usage, which opens ChatGPT's usage page.
steps.notice: To see how much is left, or to change how much YouCoded may use, press Manage usage. It opens in your browser.

steps.path: Settings → Assistant settings → Cloud providers → ChatGPT, right after the update that flips the switch
steps.headline: Anyone signed in the old way is asked once to sign in again, in plain words (your answer to question 2).
steps.changed: Instead of "Not signed in", the card says "Sign in again" and explains that ChatGPT sign-in has changed. The button is the same Sign in with ChatGPT.
steps.notice: One click, and the browser shows a ChatGPT page naming YouCoded rather than Codex. A ChatGPT message sent before that says the same thing and offers Open Settings.
steps.risk: Until they sign in again, ChatGPT models don't work for that person.

steps.path: The message under a conversation when the ChatGPT allowance runs out
steps.headline: When the allowance runs out on the official version, the message points to ChatGPT's usage page instead of a reset time.
steps.changed: OpenAI doesn't tell apps when the limit resets, or whether it's the whole plan or just YouCoded's share. So the message says what's known, and Upgrade plan becomes Manage usage.
steps.notice: Manage usage opens ChatGPT's page, where you can see when it resets or give YouCoded a bigger share. Switch Providers works as today.
steps.risk: The message no longer says when you can carry on. You find that out on ChatGPT's page.
